subject: Privileged service account lifecycle & delegated admin controls - evidence request
messages:
From: Jennifer Thomas <jennifer.thomas@everatlas.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: Procurement <procurement@everatlas.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions - privileged service accounts and delegated admin controls

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking our RFP. We have a follow-up set of technical questions focused on privileged service accounts and delegated/admin controls; these will feed into our security gating for a proof-of-concept. Can you please provide short answers and any evidence for the items below? If you have existing runbooks or diagrams, please attach.

1) Service account credential lifecycle: supported types (static keys, JWTs, short-lived tokens), rotation cadence, and automated rotation capabilities.
2) Break-glass / emergency access: how is it provisioned, approval flow, and audit trail?
3) SCIM provisioning: can we provision admin roles via group mapping? Does Redwood support SCIM v2 and bulk provisioning?
4) RBAC model: delegated admin roles for tenant admins vs platform admins — how granular are role permissions and can they be scoped to a tenant/project?
5) SSO compatibility: SAML and OIDC support, idp-initiated vs sp-initiated flows, and options to restrict login to managed users only.
6) Auditing and retention: sample of the audit logs available, retention defaults, and export options.

If possible, please include one or two short artifacts (runbook, attribute mapping, sample logs) we can include in the security review. We are on a tight timeline and would like to complete this section by next Wednesday.

Thanks,
Jennifer Thomas
Senior Security Engineer
EverAtlas
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Jennifer Thomas <jennifer.thomas@everatlas.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions - privileged service accounts and delegated admin controls

Jennifer —

Appreciate the clear list. High-level answers below and I attached a short runbook and mapping artifacts for your review. We can hop on a quick call if you want to walk through any item.

1) Service account credential lifecycle:
- Supported credential types: short-lived OAuth tokens (recommended), X.509 certs for internal k8s workloads, and HMAC API keys for legacy integrations.
- Rotation: API keys are rotatable via the Console with immediate invalidation; default recommended rotation for API keys is 90 days, but customers can enforce shorter intervals via policy. Short-lived tokens are issued with TTLs as low as 5 minutes when using our ephemeral token flow.
- Automation: We integrate with customer KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault) and support automatic key rotation hooks and webhook notifications. See attached privileged-sa-runbook.pdf for example flows.

2) Break-glass / emergency access:
- Process: Break-glass access is available as a time-bound elevation of privileges. It requires two-person approval (approver from the customer admin group + Redwood security approver for hosted deployments) and is forcibly logged.
- Controls: Elevation sessions are single-use, expire after a configurable window (default 4 hours), and write immutable audit events to the audit service and to a customer-configured SIEM via syslog/HTTP forwarders.

3) SCIM provisioning:
- SCIM version: SCIM v2 (RFC 7644) compliant.
- Group-to-role mapping: Yes — group SCIM assertions can be mapped to Redwood RBAC roles (tenant-admin, billing-operator, read-only). This mapping supports nested groups and can be pushed in bulk for initial syncs. See scim-attribute-map.csv.

4) RBAC model:
- Granularity: Roles are hierarchical and scopeable. We support resource-level scoping (project, tenant, environment) and attribute-based constraints (e.g., can_manage_models=true). Delegated admin roles can be limited to: user provisioning, billing views, model deployment approvals, or full tenant admin. Role-matrix.xlsx attached.

5) SSO compatibility:
- Protocols: Both SAML 2.0 and OIDC are supported (IdP-initiated and SP-initiated).
- Managed-only restriction: We support SCIM-based user provisioning plus SSO enforcement policies that restrict logins to users present in the SCIM provisioning set and optionally to members of a specific group (e.g., "redwood-access").

6) Auditing and retention:
- Logs: Token issuance, role changes, break-glass events, model rollouts, and admin API calls are recorded. Default retention for hosted customers is 365 days; configurable retention and exports are available. Attached is a small sample audit export (audit-log-sample.csv).

Attachments included: privileged-sa-runbook.pdf, scim-attribute-map.csv, role-matrix.xlsx, audit-log-sample.csv

Related links:
- Console docs: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/solutions/EverAtlas-PrivSA
- HubSpot record: HS-30219

If you want, Kim (copied) can provide the KMS/rotation architecture detail and a short diagram. Would you like that included?

Best,
Jonas Weber
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
(415) 555-0176
From: Jennifer Thomas <jennifer.thomas@everatlas.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: Procurement <procurement@everatlas.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions - privileged service accounts and delegated admin controls

Thanks Jonas — that helps a lot. Two quick clarifications before we move this to our risk committee:

A) For API keys and long-lived credentials, can you confirm if Redwood enforces unique key identifiers and can force rotation across all keys for a tenant (bulk revoke)? We want the ability to invalidate any compromised credentials from our Console and via API.

B) For break-glass: is the two-person approval configurable to be customer-only? Our policy prefers customer-only approvers where possible; having a Redwood approver is a blocker for our security team unless we can scope it to the customer's delegated approvers.

Also, SCIM group-mapping is great — can you confirm whether group claims from a SAML assertion can also be used at login time to derive temporary admin elevation (e.g., idp group claim triggers an elevation that still requires the break-glass approval)?

If you can send the KMS rotation architecture PDF and call out the configurable flags in the runbook, that will be perfect.

Regards,
Jennifer
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jennifer Thomas <jennifer.thomas@everatlas.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions - privileged service accounts and delegated admin controls

Jennifer —

Quick follow-up with the architecture/detail you requested. Attaching the KMS rotation architecture PDF and clarifying the three points you raised.

A) Bulk revoke / unique key IDs:
- Console/API: Tenants have the ability to list, revoke, and rotate keys via both the Console and the Admin API. Keys are issued with unique IDs and audit events are generated for create/rotate/revoke. Bulk revoke: admin API supports filter-based bulk revoke (e.g., all keys created before a date, or by tag).

B) Break-glass approver scope:
- Customer-only option: Yes. For Private/Dedicated deployments we support configuring the approver policy to require only customer-designated approvers. For hosted customers, customers can opt into a customer-only approver flow provided at least two distinct customer approvers are defined; Redwood will not be a hard approver in that case. Our default is to include a Redwood watcher for emergency contact but that can be disabled per contract.

C) Group/SAML-triggered elevation:
- At auth time we can consume group claims from SAML/OIDC assertions. We support a flow where group claims can surface an "elevation suggestion" in the Console. However, elevations that result in privileged session creation still require the break-glass approval configured for the tenant — group claims alone do not auto-elevate without explicit approvals.

Attached: kms-rotation-architecture.pdf (diagram + sequence), updated privileged-sa-runbook.pdf (callout section on configurable flags).

If you'd like, Marissa can include a short extract of audit events for a sample break-glass flow showing approver IDs (we can obfuscate PII). Let me know if that helps your committee.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Trust & Security Programs
kimberly_park@redwood.com
